claim_test: Grandchild-expanded resonant law object retrieval, synthetic seeded substrate
interpretation: Supports case-local retrieval and cross-depth composition for synthetic grandchild law objects; does not establish nested sibling.
limitations: Single synthetic seed; geometric-only residual; high resonance entropy.
next_action: Run structural family-key retrieval and compare local versus cross-seed scope.

claim_test: Grandchild-expanded resonant law object retrieval, naked_rafa CUDA local versus cross-seed
interpretation: Case-local naked_rafa retrieval passes on all three CUDA seeds, but aggregate cross-seed retrieval fails; reusable cross-anchor law identity is not established.
limitations: Short 64-step seeded assay; geometric-only retrieval; structural family labels not yet learned.
next_action: Add structural family keys and cross-seed decoy analysis.

claim_test: Operator-valued child law payload causality, naked_rafa CUDA
interpretation: Selected child law operators causally move the parent phase state beyond inert control with low world-jump proxy in naked_rafa CUDA seeds.
limitations: Short-horizon causal delta only; no proof of nested sibling or audio improvement.
next_action: Compare selected operator against decoy operator and disabled-writeback controls.

claim_test: Resonant attention contract tests after identity/composition patch
interpretation: Regression tests now cover root origin family continuity and self-parent composition filtering.
limitations: Contract tests are small and do not validate audio behavior.
next_action: Add structural family-key regression tests once implemented.

claim_test: Dual-scope retrieval: local versus structural law identity on naked_rafa CUDA
interpretation: Local case/root-child identity fails globally, but structural q/arc/support/lifecycle identity passes strongly across naked_rafa CUDA seeds.
limitations: Structural family key is deterministic bucketing, not learned ontology or runtime routing.
next_action: Train a small structural-family probe and compare learned structural retrieval against deterministic buckets.

claim_test: Selected versus decoy operator causality on naked_rafa CUDA
interpretation: Selected operator is less forceful but safer than the best wrong-family decoy; operator success should be compatibility-constrained causal movement, not maximum phase movement.
limitations: Short-horizon assay; no nested sibling conversion or audio-facing benefit yet.
next_action: Add selected-vs-decoy continuation and nested-label impact, not just immediate phase delta.

claim_test: Structural family scope regression tests
interpretation: Contract suite now verifies structural family keys are case-independent while local family keys remain case-specific.
limitations: Unit-scale only.
next_action: Add learned structural family tests after probe implementation.

claim_test: Learned structural-family probe, naked_rafa CUDA holdout 9102
interpretation: Tiny pairwise learned probe recovers cross-seed structural family agreement from law-object features while preserving local identity separation on held-out naked_seed_9102.
limitations: Teacher is deterministic structural pseudo-label; not unsupervised ontology discovery or runtime routing.
next_action: Train contrastive structural embedding without hand-bucket teacher, using cross-seed recurrence and operator safety as targets.

claim_test: Learned structural-family probe, leave-one-seed robustness
interpretation: Learned structural-family signal is stable across all three leave-one-seed folds.
limitations: All folds use same generated law-object substrate and deterministic structural labels.
next_action: Rerun on independently generated seeds and add audio-continuation/operator-safety targets.

claim_test: Law-object feature vector contract
interpretation: Contract suite now verifies learned-probe feature vector length, range, and object-kind signal.
limitations: Unit-scale only.
next_action: Add saved-checkpoint smoke load test if learned probe becomes a runtime dependency.

claim_test: Contrastive recurrence embedding synthetic smoke
interpretation: Controlled synthetic law objects verify the recurrence-trained contrastive embedding machinery and checkpoint export path.
limitations: Synthetic families are intentionally separable and do not establish real Circleworld ontology.
next_action: Run on seeded naked_rafa child/grandchild law-object substrate.

claim_test: Contrastive recurrence embedding, naked_rafa leave-one-seed
interpretation: A reusable cross-seed structural relation is learnable from continuous recurrence-compatible RAFA geometry without using structural_family_key as a training teacher.
limitations: The recurrence compatibility function is engineered RAFA geometry, not pure unsupervised discovery; the embedding is not yet used for runtime operator selection or audio continuation.
next_action: Use the learned embedding as a shadow selector in operator-causality assays and compare against recurrence-selected operators and wrong-family decoys.

claim_test: Contrastive recurrence/safety surface contract
interpretation: Contract suite now verifies recurrence compatibility and operator-safety proxy stay bounded and preserve same-child high compatibility across cases.
limitations: Unit-scale only; does not validate learned checkpoint loading.
next_action: Add checkpoint smoke-load test if the contrastive embedding becomes a reusable selector dependency.

claim_test: Operator causality selector contract: non-self selected operator and learned shadow selector
interpretation: The operator assay now compares non-self selected, recurrence-selected, learned-hybrid-selected, and wrong-family decoy operators while keeping runtime Circleworld unchanged.
limitations: Assay behavior changed versus prior reports because the older selected path could apply the query object itself.
next_action: Reinterpret selected-vs-decoy operator causality with the corrected non-self selector.

claim_test: Learned contrastive embedding as shadow operator selector on naked_rafa
interpretation: The learned recurrence embedding is not yet safe as an operator router: it consistently selects the wrong-family decoy even with a capped nonnegative learned residual.
limitations: Only three seeded naked_rafa cases on one checkpoint/config; learned selector used a checkpoint trained as retrieval embedding, not causal operator selector.
next_action: Train the selector on causal-safe operator labels or add a stricter recurrence/identity membrane before allowing learned residual to influence routing.

claim_test: Learned operator routing membrane and causal selector probe
interpretation: Learned residual is now gated by a recurrence/identity membrane in the assay path, and a separate causal selector can train on actual candidate writeback outcomes.
limitations: Assay-only; causal selector checkpoint is not consumed by production Circleworld.
next_action: Scale causal candidate collection across more seeds/configs before considering a learned branch-law runtime path.

claim_test: Causal operator selector trained on actual writeback outcomes
interpretation: Causal labels give a better operator-routing objective than retrieval similarity: the membrane-selected causal router mostly preserves identity while approaching the target-top candidate score.
limitations: Only 126 candidate rows from three seeds; target includes engineered identity membrane and is not yet a learned branch law.
next_action: Generate a larger causal label bank and compare causal-selector residual against recurrence-only routing.

claim_test: Retrieval-learned selector rerun with recurrence/identity membrane
interpretation: The retrieval-trained selector becomes safe as a shadow residual only when subordinated to the identity/recurrence membrane; without the membrane it chose the wrong-family decoy.
limitations: The learned residual did not yet demonstrate a useful novel operator choice; the guard mostly forces agreement with geometric/recurrence routing.
next_action: Train and evaluate a causal-selector residual that can improve over membrane-only routing without violating identity.

claim_test: Assay-only causal selector residual route
interpretation: The operator causality assay can now consume a causal selector checkpoint and report a shadow geometric_score + causal_selector_residual route.
limitations: Assay-only and still membrane-gated; no Circleworld runtime branch law behavior changed.
next_action: Use the route to compare causal residuals across larger and harder causal-label banks.

claim_test: Scaled causal operator selector label bank, 12 naked_rafa seeds
interpretation: Causal operator labels scale to 504 candidate rows while preserving identity-compatible holdout routing close to the target-top score.
limitations: Still one config, one warmup/depth regime, and engineered causal target.
next_action: Generate causal labels across multiple configs and grandchild depths.

claim_test: Causal selector checkpoint on unseen naked_rafa seeds with residual-only control
interpretation: The causal residual can lift the identity-compatible candidate above a higher-geometry wrong-family decoy on unseen seeds, which is the first useful learned-routing behavior beyond a pure membrane guard.
limitations: The effect is modest and the residual is still membrane-gated; not ready for runtime promotion.
next_action: Create harder decoy controls and train a multi-head causal selector over movement, world-jump risk, identity carry, and route score.

claim_test: Multi-head causal operator selector contract
interpretation: Causal operator routing now has a shared multi-head selector contract and assay support for movement, jump-safety, identity, and route-score heads.
limitations: Assay-only; no Circleworld runtime branch law changes.
next_action: Use multi-head outputs to build a shadow learned branch-law table.

claim_test: Depth-2 multi-head causal operator selector, trained phasor authority config
interpretation: Depth-2 creates harder decoys: wrong-family decoys move the parent more but worsen world-jump risk. The multi-head causal selector chooses the branch-authorized lower-jump operator.
limitations: Trained and tested within one config family; no cross-config checkpoint transfer yet.
next_action: Evaluate the same checkpoint on a different config without retraining.

claim_test: Alternate childphase config depth-2 multi-head causal selector
interpretation: The alternate childphase config repeats the safe-authority pattern: the causal selector chooses lower-jump branch-authorized operators over higher-movement wrong-family decoys.
limitations: This is per-config training, not cross-config generalization.
next_action: Add hard-decoy summary metrics and cross-config checkpoint transfer tests.

claim_test: Hard-decoy accounting for causal operator routing
interpretation: The assay now distinguishes high-movement wrong-family decoys from branch-authorized lower-jump operators.
limitations: Instrumentation only; does not change Circleworld runtime routing.
next_action: Use hard-decoy metrics as targets for learned branch-law training.

claim_test: Cross-config causal selector transfer, phasor-authority to childphase and reverse
interpretation: The learned causal selector transfers across two nearby ontology configs and keeps selecting the branch-authorized lower-jump operator over higher-movement hard decoys.
limitations: The configs are closely related and produce near-identical outcome surfaces; broader transfer remains unproven.
next_action: Evaluate shadow law on wider config families and depths.

claim_test: Shadow branch-law table from causal operator-routing outputs
interpretation: Causal routing evidence is now expressed as continuous branch-law fields suitable for training an assay-only learned branch law.
limitations: Fields are engineered from current assay outputs, not yet learned end-to-end or validated as runtime updates.
next_action: Train a tiny learned branch-law head on these fields and evaluate it in shadow mode.

claim_test: Shadow branch-law trainer using existing RafaLearnedBranchLawV0
interpretation: Added an assay-only trainer that maps shadow causal-routing rows into the existing learned branch-law output schema.
limitations: Uses engineered shadow fields, not raw runtime branch-law discovery.
next_action: Use the checkpoint as a shadow validator on fresh measured causality rows.

claim_test: Wider depth-3 causality probes on authority and no-delta ontology configs
interpretation: Depth-3 creates a negative writeback regime: the causal route moves more but jumps more, so safety/authority wins disappear.
limitations: Two configs are still near-family and produced identical aggregate surfaces on these seeds.
next_action: Evaluate distant configs and real-anchor substrates.

claim_test: Expanded mixed shadow branch-law table and learned fit
interpretation: The existing learned branch-law module can fit mixed assay-derived branch fields including denied writeback regimes.
limitations: Low error is expected because targets are engineered and table is small; not runtime evidence.
next_action: Predict branch-law fields on fresh causality assays before table conversion and measure calibration.

claim_test: Shadow branch-law calibration evaluator
interpretation: Added an upstream calibration evaluator that predicts learned branch-law fields from raw causality assay rows before table aggregation.
limitations: Still uses shadow-row target construction for measured labels after prediction.
next_action: Use learned-gated writeback in a reversible sandbox assay.

claim_test: Fresh positive and negative causality slices for branch-law calibration
interpretation: Fresh unseen seeds reproduce the intended split: depth-2 permits safe writeback while depth-3 denies jumpier writeback.
limitations: Same nearby config family; not a distant distribution shift.
next_action: Run the same calibration on real-anchor/fallback configs.

claim_test: Learned shadow branch-law calibration against raw causality rows
interpretation: The learned shadow branch-law checkpoint predicts survival/collapse/writeback fields accurately on fresh raw causality rows and separates positive from negative writeback regimes at threshold 0.78.
limitations: Writeback score is not calibrated probability; negative rows remain high-scoring but below threshold.
next_action: Build a sandbox learned-gated writeback assay and compare against ungated child-local IFS.

claim_test: Learned-gated writeback sandbox script and contract
interpretation: Added a reversible operator-level sandbox where learned branch-law outputs gate measured child writeback permission.
limitations: Does not modify circleworld_step and does not test multi-step runtime dynamics.
next_action: Add soft attenuation gate and compare retained parent divergence against jump reduction.

claim_test: Learned gate intervention on fresh depth-2/depth-3 causality rows
interpretation: The learned gate preserves all safe depth-2 returns and suppresses all unsafe depth-3 returns on fresh seeds.
limitations: Hard denial removes all parent influence from denied children; no partial law modulation yet.
next_action: Run a soft-gated sandbox using continuous writeback score.

claim_test: Safety interpretation of hard learned gating
interpretation: The learned branch law is currently useful as a safety filter, not yet as a nuanced branch dynamics controller.
limitations: Operator-level sandbox only; no nested sibling/audio proof.
next_action: Graduate from binary safety gate to soft learned writeback attenuation.

claim_test: Soft learned writeback gate implementation and contract
interpretation: The learned-gated sandbox now supports continuous writeback attenuation via soft floor/full score controls.
limitations: Operator-level sandbox only; still not multi-step runtime branch control.
next_action: Apply soft floor 0.70 in a multi-step sandbox.

claim_test: Soft gate sweep over floors 0.60, 0.65, 0.70
interpretation: Lower soft floors retain more parent influence but admit more world-jump; higher floors approach hard-gate safety.
limitations: World-jump and divergence are linearly scaled operator proxies, not full recurrent dynamics.
next_action: Test soft floor 0.70 under actual multi-step recurrence.

claim_test: Hard-vs-soft gate tradeoff comparison
interpretation: Soft floor 0.70 is the best immediate candidate: near-hard safety with a small nonzero amount of denied-child influence retained.
limitations: The gain over hard is small and may vanish in runtime recurrence.
next_action: Use floor 0.70 as the default soft-gate setting for the next sandbox.

claim_test: Multi-step learned-gated operator recurrence script and contract
interpretation: Added a regenerated-state multi-step operator recurrence sandbox for learned hard/soft gates.
limitations: Still operator-level recurrence, not full circleworld_step runtime gating.
next_action: Add true assay-only runtime hook before child writeback.

claim_test: Depth-2 safe-regime multi-step recurrence with hard/soft/ungated gates
interpretation: Safe depth-2 child returns are nearly preserved under soft floor 0.70/full 0.88 across four recurrent operator applications.
limitations: Depth-2 repeated operator recurrence amplifies jump relative to one-step proxies.
next_action: Check whether full runtime recurrence keeps this safe-regime transparency.

claim_test: Depth-3 unsafe-regime multi-step recurrence with hard/soft/ungated gates
interpretation: Unsafe depth-3 soft gating preserves a small amount of parent movement while eliminating final world-jump in the operator recurrence model.
limitations: Huge influence-per-jump ratio is caused by zero final jump denominator and should not be overinterpreted.
next_action: Move to full runtime sandbox gating where children can evolve after each step.

claim_test: Assay-only learned child writeback scale hook in circleworld_step
interpretation: Learned branch-law outputs can now be routed into actual Circleworld child writeback as an assay-only scale without changing default runtime behavior.
limitations: The hook is a scalar child-return gate, not yet a full learned split/merge/survival law replacing parametric branch updates.
next_action: Test the hook in controlled runtime recurrence.

claim_test: Depth-2 carrier runtime recurrence with learned gate
interpretation: The learned branch law permits depth-2 carrier return, and that return causally moves the parent above the blocked runtime baseline.
limitations: Safe return also increases world-jump proxy; permissive depth-2 needs downstream continuity/audio checks before promotion.
next_action: Run many-child ecology to see whether safe carriers remain useful when competing children coexist.

claim_test: Depth-3 authority runtime recurrence with learned hard/soft gate
interpretation: The learned branch law hard-blocks risky depth-3 authority return; soft gating preserves a small runtime child influence while reducing jump relative to ungated.
limitations: Selected-child sandbox only; negative jump lift versus blocked reflects nonlinear runtime interaction and needs replication in many-child ecology.
next_action: Generalize from isolated selected child to all live child worlds with per-child learned scales.

claim_test: Many-child learned runtime writeback sandbox
interpretation: Added a many-child ecology sandbox where every live child receives an assay-only writeback scale before each actual circleworld_step call.
limitations: Per-child score construction is still a proxy based on query-to-candidate law-object rows and does not yet implement global authority allocation.
next_action: Run soft70 and strict88 many-child ecology comparisons.

claim_test: Soft70 many-child ecology runtime
interpretation: Soft70 attenuates many-child jump relative to ungated but remains too permissive at depth 3 because many children receive high independent scales.
limitations: Many-child scorer lacks support-overlap budget and sibling competition, so children are not forced to compete for parent authority.
next_action: Increase the soft floor/threshold and inspect whether jump can be held near blocked baseline.

claim_test: Strict88 many-child ecology runtime
interpretation: Strict88 soft gating is the first useful many-child setting: nonzero child writeback with jump near blocked baseline. Hard thresholding still over-permits children, showing the need for authority allocation rather than independent permission.
limitations: Strict soft return has negative parent lift versus blocked, suggesting stabilizing cancellation rather than clear sibling-development authority.
next_action: Implement ecology-level writeback budget allocation across overlapping child supports.

claim_test: Ecology-level authority allocator variants
interpretation: Added support-overlap and redundancy-aware authority allocation on top of learned many-child writeback scales.
limitations: Allocator acts as an assay-time scalar scale, not an in-model learned allocation network.
next_action: Run allocator on Soft70 and Strict88 many-child substrates.

claim_test: Conservative ecology allocator over many-child substrates
interpretation: Conservative allocation eliminates world-jump but over-damps child authority because overlap load dominates the budget.
limitations: This result is safe but too close to blocking; it does not prove sibling-development authority.
next_action: Try a looser allocation profile to retain more nonzero child return.

claim_test: Loose ecology allocator profile and stabilizer interpretation
interpretation: Loose allocation preserves more child writeback than conservative allocation while keeping jump at zero in depth-3 probes, but the parent lift remains negative, suggesting stabilizing/canceling authority rather than developmental sibling authority.
limitations: Only three naked_rafa seeds and proxy world-jump metrics; no downstream audio or nested_sibling verdict yet.
next_action: Add a developmental-authority objective that rewards safe positive parent lift separately from stabilizing cancellation.

claim_test: Developmental authority allocator variant
interpretation: Added an assay-only allocator profile that explicitly rewards safe parent movement, not only stabilizing jump suppression.
limitations: Still scalar allocation over children; it does not yet cluster vector return directions.
next_action: Run developmental allocator on same many-child substrates.

claim_test: Developmental allocator many-child runtime runs
interpretation: Developmental allocator keeps zero jump and preserves slightly more writeback than the loose stabilizer, but parent lift remains negative.
limitations: Only three seeds and proxy parent-lift/jump metrics; no nested verdict yet.
next_action: Inspect directional alignment of child phase-return vectors.

claim_test: Safe but not developmental child ecology
interpretation: The child ecology problem is now identified as directional coherence, not just volume, threshold, hard/soft gating, or budget allocation. Individually lawful child returns cancel/stabilize when combined unless a coherent return direction is selected.
limitations: Directional coalition allocator not implemented yet.
next_action: Implement directional_child_coalition_allocator_v0 as an assay-only many-child variant.

claim_test: Directional child coalition allocator variants
interpretation: Added assay-only child-return vector coalition selection to test whether many-child cancellation was caused by anti-aligned return directions.
limitations: Coalition target is mutual alignment only, not alignment to an externally derived sibling-development direction.
next_action: Run directional coalition over the many-child substrates.

claim_test: Directional child coalition allocator runtime runs
interpretation: Mutual directional alignment gets closest to safe positive parent lift, but still remains slightly negative; it is safer and less cancelling than scalar developmental allocation in depth-2 Strict88.
limitations: Still no positive parent-development lift; proxy parent divergence may not equal true sibling ontology.
next_action: Test whether boosted aligned coalition crosses into positive lift or jump.

claim_test: Boosted directional coalition check
interpretation: Boosting the aligned coalition increases child writeback but worsens stabilization/cancellation, proving the selected aligned direction is not the desired developmental direction.
limitations: No target-conditioned sibling direction was supplied, so the coalition can only choose mutual coherence.
next_action: Implement target_conditioned_child_coalition_allocator_v0.

claim_test: Endogenous target-conditioned child coalition allocator
interpretation: Added an assay-only target-conditioned coalition allocator using a tangent-to-collapse target derived from child return vectors.
limitations: Target is endogenous to the same child ecology being allocated, not an external sibling continuation target.
next_action: Run target-conditioned allocator on the same substrates.

claim_test: Target-conditioned child coalition runtime runs
interpretation: Target conditioning increased target projection and writeback but still produced negative parent lift with zero jump. The target was aligned but stabilizing.
limitations: No exogenous sibling target was used; this does not rule out target-conditioned allocation using controlled sibling deltas.
next_action: Build contrastive_sibling_target_allocator_v0.

claim_test: Endogenous target fails to create sibling-development authority
interpretation: The child ecology now needs an exogenous or contrastive sibling target. Endogenous targets derived from child returns select stabilizing tangent fields rather than true sibling continuation directions.
limitations: World-jump and parent-lift remain proxy metrics; nested verdict not rerun.
next_action: Derive blocked-to-controlled-sibling target directions and rerun coalition selection.

claim: Controlled tangent sibling target variant was added to avoid endogenous target circularity.
interpretation: Allocation now tests projection onto an external sibling-development direction rather than child-field self-alignment.

claim: Existing many-child banks can project onto exogenous sibling targets.
interpretation: Target projections were only about 0.004-0.006, so learned allocation becomes safe but nearly inert.

claim: Many-child failure is primarily scalar gate/allocation instability.
interpretation: The sharper bottleneck is child operator-basis coverage: current children are coherent but not aligned to sibling-development directions.

claim: Child-bank target coverage should be measured before more allocation tuning.
interpretation: A dedicated assay now reports basis rank, target projection, coverage fractions, and contrastive runtime recurrence for natural and target-augmented child banks.

claim: Natural child banks have no projection onto the allocator-exact sibling target.
interpretation: Best natural target projection is around 0.112, but only a small fraction of children clear useful thresholds, so coverage is sparse rather than absent.

claim: Target-aligned child carriers are sufficient for parent-visible sibling writeback.
interpretation: Synthetic target augmentation raises target projection sharply, but learned allocation keeps writeback tiny; the next objective must jointly train coverage and authority.

claim: Target-aligned children need stronger authority than the conservative contrastive allocator gives them.
interpretation: Added assay-only target-authority allocator with authority floors for children that project onto controlled sibling targets.

claim: Authority variants must be compared against a local blocked baseline.
interpretation: The assay now runs blocked_zero for each natural/augmented phase and computes variant-specific parent and jump lift.

claim: Giving target-aligned children authority is sufficient for clean sibling ontology.
interpretation: Authority produces parent-visible movement, but also increases world-jump; learned supervision must jointly optimize target projection, movement, and coarse identity preservation.

claim: Phase-native audio viability needs a first-class testing-suite wrapper separate from child ontology and resonant memory assays.
interpretation: Added an additive dry-run/run suite for copyphase no-future continuation and fixed prefix-only phase-delta probes, with a shared scorecard contract.

claim: The audio reset should be visible in the DAG/report lane without becoming a new canonical architecture node.
interpretation: Registered phase_native_audio_reset_v1 as a documentation-only testing overlay and optional runtime-manifest entrypoint; no existing DAG node or JSON key was renamed.

claim: The new suite wiring is executable enough to produce a dry-run command manifest and scorecard shell.
interpretation: The dry run wrote planned commands and promotion criteria only. It is not an audio result and does not change the prior negative/weak phase-native audio viability read.

claim: The registered phase-native audio reset suite can execute a one-case CPU smoke run and classify promotion status from real child artifacts.
interpretation: All child commands completed and future-access flags were clean. The smoke case showed positive mean corr delta versus copy-last and prefix/copyphase, but failed promotion because MSE and first-chunk reentry worsened versus copy-last.

claim: A fresh full phase-native audio lockbox can be predeclared from the local WAV pool before outcome evaluation.
interpretation: The builder selected 62 cases across 10 predeclared groups with no unmet minimum groups using seed 20260517; this freezes the full reset-suite substrate.

claim: Circleworld phase-native continuation can pass the full lockbox promotion contract against copy-last and copyphase carriers.
interpretation: The full lockbox run was future-access clean and improved aggregate corr, MSE, and loop peak versus copy-last, but failed because first-chunk reentry worsened by about 0.0469 versus copy-last.

claim: The best full-lockbox phase-delta mechanism is robust rather than outlier/family dominated.
interpretation: Best mechanism row was phase_router_bins/time_smooth_3/gain2 with mean corr delta about 0.0245 but median only 0.0000277 and win fraction 0.516; excluding razor and buzzy-synth shrinks mean corr delta to about 0.0010.

claim: The full lockbox failure should be scored against copy-last reentry directly, not only gain-0 carrier deltas.
interpretation: Added a reentry-guard scorer joining delta rows to copy-last baselines across all/no-razor/no-buzzy views; the original full-lockbox grid had zero strict or diagnostic reentry-guard candidates.

claim: A legal no-future phase seed policy can remove the first-chunk reentry failure versus copy-last.
interpretation: The seed ablation shows seed policy matters and can improve corr/MSE, but joined scoring against copy-last found zero strict rows; best rows still have positive reentry deltas around 0.045 to 0.068.

claim: Prefix-phase anti-reentry shear can reduce the reentry failure enough to pass the copy-last guard.
interpretation: Added phase-only anti_reentry shear mechanisms. The first shear probe found native gain-0 mechanism candidates and reduced reentry versus gain-0, but copy-last reentry guard scoring still found zero strict candidates.

claim: Increasing anti-reentry shear gain will cross the copy-last reentry threshold without destroying corr/MSE/loop gains.
interpretation: High-gain shear preserved useful corr/MSE/loop movement, but reentry delta versus copy-last remained positive; best all-view guard row still had reentry delta about +0.0427.

claim: The reentry failure may be solvable by a learned selector/router over existing phase-delta rows.
interpretation: Added a global/family/case oracle over the original, shear, and high-gain grids. Even case-oracle routing across 27652 rows failed the strict copy-last reentry guard, so the next step needs new operator capacity or a refined reentry metric contract.

claim: Case-oracle routing can pass phase-native audio reentry while preserving corr/MSE/loop gains.
interpretation: Case oracle improved corr by about +0.0887, MSE by -0.0294, and loop by -0.0893 versus copy-last, but reentry remained positive at about +0.0199; selector-only is insufficient.

claim: The copy-last reentry failure may be an artifact of stationary targets where high self-similarity is lawful.
interpretation: Target-normalized audit shows Circleworld matches the target reentry profile better than copy-last, but still has higher harmful replay excess than copy-last by about +0.00716.

claim: A later-chunk deterministic phase decorrelator can beat copy-last reentry without losing corr/MSE/loop gains.
interpretation: Late/staggered/decorrelator-mix mechanisms reduced some reentry metrics and produced tradeoff rows, but copy-last guard scoring still found zero strict candidates.

claim: Adding late decorrelators gives enough operator capacity for a case-oracle reentry pass.
interpretation: Oracle plus decorrelator improved global reentry delta to about +0.0245 and case-oracle corr to about +0.0975, but case-oracle reentry remained positive at about +0.0198; new objective/operator capacity is still needed.

claim: Target-normalized harmful replay should be scored as excess over the real future's own first-chunk reentry rather than as a raw self-similarity scalar.
interpretation: Added a target replay oracle scorer and registered it in the runtime manifest so phase-native audio reentry can be evaluated against target-like stationarity instead of only the copy-last first-chunk guard.

claim: The current phase-only mechanism pool contains enough anti-replay capacity if routing is evaluated with target-normalized harmful replay excess.
interpretation: Across 42532 rows, global routing still fails, but family-level routing passes: corr +0.05563, MSE -0.02838, loop -0.12353, harmful replay excess delta -0.00243 versus copy-last, and corr versus gain0 +0.04634. This is an oracle ceiling, not a deployable policy; next step is a prefix-only family/router policy.

claim: A target-normalized anti-replay route may be recoverable from legal prefix-only Circleworld metadata rather than only from oracle access to future metrics.
interpretation: Added a prefix-router scout. On the full lockbox, known-family routing, leave-one-case nearest-case routing, and leave-one-case family-centroid routing all pass the strict target-normalized replay guard. Leave-one-group routing remains non-promotional because corr versus gain0 is negative.

claim: Prefix/Circleworld metadata can select anti-replay phase-only routes that preserve corr/MSE/loop gains while reducing target-normalized harmful replay excess.
interpretation: Leave-one-case nearest-case policy: corr +0.02722, MSE -0.02354, loop -0.06013, harmful replay excess delta -0.00605, corr-gain0 +0.01426. Leave-one-case family-centroid policy: corr +0.02576, MSE -0.02490, loop -0.14108, harmful replay excess delta -0.00740, corr-gain0 +0.01368. This is a scout over existing rendered rows, not yet a live runtime router or fresh-lockbox validation.

claim: The prefix-router result must be validated on a fresh deterministic lockbox rather than only the original 20260517 case set.
interpretation: Built a fresh predeclared lockbox with seed 20260518, preserving the 62-case group structure and no target-metric selection. A first accidental 3-case default run was treated as smoke-only and excluded from evidence.

claim: The raw phase-native audio reset suite should remain honest on a fresh full lockbox before route-specific scoring.
interpretation: Fresh full raw suite remains non-promotional because first-chunk reentry worsens by about +0.0480, but corr improves by +0.00939, MSE by -0.02401, and loop peak by -0.01262 versus copy-last.

claim: The target-normalized anti-replay oracle should survive a fresh full lockbox.
interpretation: On the fresh 62-case lockbox, the global target replay route passes: corr +0.03506, MSE -0.02433, loop -0.01494, harmful replay excess delta -0.00255, corr-gain0 +0.03606. Family and case oracles also pass.

claim: No-future prefix-feature routing should survive fresh full lockbox validation.

claim: Original-lockbox family routes should survive as live selected-route rendering on the fresh lockbox.

claim: Fresh-lockbox global route should survive as live selected-route rendering on the original lockbox.

claim: Fresh-lockbox family table should survive as live selected-route rendering on the original lockbox.

claim: Explicit no-future family identification may recover robust family-conditioned route selection better than direct route prediction.
interpretation: Added a family-route policy trainer that predicts family from Circleworld/prefix metadata and maps predicted family to a frozen source family route table. Models include group centroid, kNN1, and kNN5.

claim: A no-future family-prediction route policy can pass the third lockbox where direct learned route policies failed.

claim: Objective-aware learned routing should beat the frozen family table on all dimensions.

claim: The frozen objective_knn5_v1 component must pass no-future, source-target separation, metric, and raw-Circleworld guard audits.

claim: Routed Circleworld objective_knn5 should be compared against raw Circleworld and the current compat14 adapter on one shared lockbox battlefield.

interpretation: Added circleworld_operator_block_v1, which uses prefix/Circleworld route policy input, the canonical operator bank, phase wrapping/unit-phasor contracts, selected-route rendering, target-normalized scoring, and raw/selected-reference comparisons.

claim: The new Circleworld operator block should execute as a no-future CPU smoke path before full lockbox evaluation.
interpretation: The 3-case CPU smoke returned operator_block_target_replay_pass with future_access_clean true, validating the basic block runner and route-policy integration.

claim: The selected-route renderer should be reproducible through the extracted canonical operator bank before comparing the new block against it.

claim: circleworld_operator_block_v1 should reproduce the canonical objective_knn5 selected-route path and beat raw Circleworld on the fourth lockbox.

This is an internal Circleworld architecture consolidation, not a raw-Circleworld promotion or Graduation comparison.
